text.p: The Baltic state of Lithuania plans a telephone hotline for alleged cases of corruption as part of its fight against graft and rising crime.
"This hotline is part of the government's 'clean hands' policy," a spokesman for the government said on Tuesday.
He said that anyone who suspected a state official of being corrupt could report the person on the hotline five days a week.
The announcement came a day after the country's prosecutor general said he was resigning because he could not cope with the rising crime rate in the Baltic state.
The country's new right-wing Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius, who was elected three months ago, has pledged to take a tough line on crime.
Lithuania was the only one of three Baltic states to show a rise in crime last year. The number of incidents rose by 11.9 percent to 68,053, the bulk of which were related to theft.
